I wish I had progress pics but alas I do not. The table is built around the top of an old $100 walmart pool table. I removed the base first, and then the metal pockets, and finally the inside rubber.

The wood I used is all cherry and came from a downed tree on a friend and fellow gamer's property which he had rough sawn into boards. We borrowed a planer and trimmed and planed the boards ourselves. The wood is so frickin beautiful and easily my favorite thing about the table.

First I nailed up the inside frame, and then the top rails flush with those. The top rails are pocket joined at the corners, and face nailed to the old pool table rails. Then i added new fascia on the outside to help support the overhang and make the rails stronger since i knew there would be lots of leaning on them. I mitered some smaller pieces to cover the outside fascia corners because my joints weren't particularly even.

The top was made by cutting a piece of 1/2" mdf to fit, then covering it with 1/4" headliner foam and some cool faux suede material from Joann's Fabrics, and then set down into the table. It can easily be popped back out for recovering if necessary.

The cherry wood was given many coats of polycrylic finish, and the finished table top was set over an old heavy duty shop table which i had in my garage..i.t fit perfectly so no sliding, though i left the old hinges from the pool table attached to the underside so that if i wanted i could screw those to the shop table.

The whole thing is loosely based off Wil Wheaton's table on the Tabletop youtube series, but with a wider rail for resting your arms. Its not a fine piece of woodworking to be sure, as I face nailed the hell out of it to make sure it was solid, and then just filled the nail holes with putty before finishing, but i am so happy with how it turned out.

The room itself is another project...a partially finished basement room which i've overhauled to fix the original shoddy construction (new reframed and larger door, ceiling taken down, soffit replaced, 40" tv with chromecast and of course new paint. Just need some more shelves, and baseboard/crown/door molding.

EDIT: Forgot to mention I used a router for the first time to smooth the outer and inner edges of the top rail. My friend did most of it, but then i did some as well. The first router bit actually broke as we were doing the inside, and left a big gouge in the wood. I colored some wood putty with acrylic paints i had on hand to match the color of the knots in the wood, and then filled the gouge and shaped it with sandpaper until it looked totally natural.

What a beautiful table. Well done!

Question for curiosity's sake; did you consider making cup-recesses so that the other gamers don't spill drinks all over that wonderful cherry wood? Or is that something that just wouldn't be worth the amount of tools/work required?

I had planned on using a holesaw to make holes for cupholders on the top, but because i facenailed so much(fascia boards), im afraid ill start cutting and hit nails and ruin the wood. Im fine with people just setting their drinks on the top though. It's about 7.5" wide so lots of room. And if necessary i can sand and refinish every year or 2 easy enough.
Also..its so damn comfortable to rest your arms on the finished wood, I'd hate to ruin that with metal.

I'm no carpenter, but I feel like it wouldn't be too hard to fasten some plastic cup holders to the sides or attach them from the bottom of the ledges. I mean, its totally not necessary. Just a thought.

I've considered that as well. Slideouts, rotate out etc. But I didnt want anything sticking out from underneath that would get in anyones way. I do think its safe to put some flip down cupholders on the exterior corners, so I could fit 8 there(2 per corner) and may do that. If i had 8 people around the table only the middle persons on the two long sides wouldn't have access to one.
